speaker: Surveyor 3
text: My engines would not shut off.

speaker: Surveyor 3
text: I bounced across the Moon. Twice. Then I was still.

speaker: Surveyor 3
text: For fourteen days I watched the Sun cross the sky. Then the night came.

speaker: Surveyor 3
text: A night on the Moon lasts two weeks. I did not survive it.

speaker: Surveyor 3
text: Thirty-one months later, I had visitors.

speaker: Surveyor 3
text: They took my eye home with them.

speaker: Surveyor 3
text: Of all of us, I am the only one they ever came back for.

speaker: Eagle
text: Six hundred million people watched me land.

speaker: Eagle
text: They called me Eagle.

speaker: Eagle
text: Two men climbed down my ladder and stepped into history.

speaker: Eagle
text: Twenty-one hours later, they left.

speaker: Eagle
text: The blast from my other half knocked their flag into the dust.

speaker: Eagle
text: I stayed. That was always the plan.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: I was the last car on the Moon.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: They drove me thirty-five kilometres through a valley no one had ever seen.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: On the last day, they parked me facing their lander, and pointed my camera at it.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: On Earth, a man named Ed Fendell held the controls.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: Radio takes time to cross that distance. He had to move my camera before the engine fired.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: He timed it perfectly.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: That was the last time a human being left the Moon.

speaker: Lunar Rover
text: I have been watching the empty sky ever since.

speaker: The Mirrors
text: In 1977, they switched off the instruments around me. To save money.

speaker: The Mirrors
text: I was never switched on. I need no power.

speaker: The Mirrors
text: I am a panel of glass mirrors, built to do one thing.

speaker: The Mirrors
text: Send back any light you give me.

speaker: The Mirrors
text: Fifty-seven years later, Earth is still knocking.

speaker: The Mirrors
text: I still answer.

speaker: The Mirrors
text: Because of me, you know the Moon drifts 3.8 centimetres farther from you every year.

speaker: Sojourner
text: I was ten kilograms of hope.

speaker: Sojourner
text: They gave me seven days.

speaker: Sojourner
text: I gave them eighty-three.

speaker: Sojourner
text: I could not speak to Earth. My lander spoke for me.

speaker: Sojourner
text: Then my lander went quiet.

speaker: Sojourner
text: If I ever lost contact, I was told to return to it. To circle it. And wait.

speaker: Sojourner
text: No one knows when I stopped.

speaker: Spirit
text: My twin landed on the far side of the planet. We never met.

speaker: Spirit
text: They gave me ninety days. I gave them six years.

speaker: Spirit
text: When one of my wheels broke, I drove backwards, dragging it behind me.

speaker: Spirit
text: These are my tracks. This is where they end.

speaker: Spirit
text: In 2009, the ground gave way beneath me. I dug. I sank.

speaker: Spirit
text: Winter was coming, and I could not turn to face the Sun.

speaker: Spirit
text: So I went to sleep, to stay warm.

speaker: Spirit
text: That was March 22, 2010. I am still asleep.
